clue.text: Dodgy character stole flash motor

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady figure has pinched a showy car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' signals rearranging the fourteen letters of CHARACTER STOLE. A Chelsea tractor is British slang for a big four-wheel-drive car driven around posh parts of London, like Chelsea, where nobody needs one.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term mocks an expensive, showy off-road vehicle used only for city driving, so it is a flashy car.

clue.text: Shackle Cinders? Novel Twist! (that was one of his)

definitions.text: Shackle Cinders? Novel Twist! (that was one of his)

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of the two words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a surprising plot twist, with a nod to a famous book title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' signals rearranging SHACKLE CINDERS. 'Twist' also points to Oliver Twist, one of the author's novels, so the whole clue describes him as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist wrote Oliver Twist, which the clue's capitalised Twist names as one of his works.

clue.text: A cheesy individual in a waxed jacket, James shelled soy beans

parts.words: A cheesy individual in a waxed jacket
parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese sold as a single round coated in red wax

indicators.note: shelled means the outer letters of James are stripped off, as a pea loses its pod

explanation.surface: A cheesy chap in a Barbour-style jacket called James has been podding soybeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cheesy individual in a waxed jacket' reads as a person but is a cheese in its wax coat. 'shelled' takes the first and last letters off JAMES, leaving AME.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are young green soybeans served in or out of the pod, a Japanese snack.

clue.text: Asking her out is a withering experience!

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plucking up courage to ask a woman on a date can end in humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'asking her out' (inviting her on a date) but signals rearranging ASKING HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Withering means drying up and getting smaller, and the noun for getting smaller is a loss in size.

clue.text: Scope no.1 climbing target

parts.note: ambit means scope or range

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters go upwards, read backwards

parts.note: no. is the abbreviation for number, and 1 is the letter I

explanation.surface: A sniper adjusts the scope on a target for the top climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no.1' reads as 'number one', but it is NO and I, which 'climbing' reverses to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition is a goal you aim at, so a target in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Up-and-coming épicerie that is missing a few ingredients?

definitions.text: Up-and-coming épicerie that is missing a few ingredients?

indicators.note: up-and-coming in a down clue means the letters rise, so they are read backwards
missing means the letters for 'that is' are dropped

parts.note: an épicerie is a French grocery shop

explanation.surface: A trendy new delicatessen is short of a few items on its shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: An épicerie is a French grocer. 'missing' takes away the letters for 'that is', and 'Up-and-coming' reads what is left upwards. A shop short of goods also hints at a list of ingredients, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructions for a dish start by listing the ingredients needed, so it is a set of a few ingredients.

clue.text: Firm support in emergency meeting

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A company stands behind its staff during a crisis summit.
explanation.walkthrough: COBRA (Cabinet Office Briefing Room A) is the British government's emergency committee, convened during national crises.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is used for the crisis committee of senior UK ministers and officials gathered when disaster strikes.

clue.text: Wearing specs, German turning over a new leaf

indicators.note: wearing means the specs go around the other pieces, as glasses sit on a face

parts.note: a pair of spectacles looks like two letter Os side by side

indicators.note: turning over means the abbreviation for German is reversed

explanation.surface: A bespectacled German is making a fresh start in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over a new leaf' is an idiom for reforming, but 'leaf' alone is the definition. 'turning over' reverses only the German abbreviation, and 'Wearing' puts the lot inside the specs.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb whose leaves are used in cooking, so it is a culinary leaf.

clue.text: Sign setter might be out of control?

definitions.text: Sign setter might be out of control?

parts.words: Sign setter might be out of control?
parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog, so a notice on a gate warns visitors that such an animal might be unruly; the crossword setter is the false reading

explanation.surface: A notice suggests the crossword compiler has lost the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' wants to be the crossword compiler; it is the dog breed, and the sign warns that the animal inside might attack.
explanation.definitionFit: The familiar gate notice warns callers about a guard animal, here a setter that might run wild.

clue.text: Back in Quebec, I bore an amniocentesis without needing oxygen

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of clue words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman recalls giving birth back in Quebec after an antenatal test.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word; it is the signal that the letters lie within the words, while 'Back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaerobic organisms or processes can live or run with no air, so they do not require oxygen.

clue.text: Note English verb (reflexive)

indicators.note: reflexive suggests turning back on itself, so the letters are reversed

explanation.surface: A grammar memo about English reflexive verbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflexive' looks like grammar, but here it means turned back, reversing E and VERB.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note worth two semibreves, rarely seen in modern scores.

clue.text: Father of 7 exposed new master

parts.note: Regan, a daughter of King Lear, lies exposed inside the answer to clue 7, so her father is meant

explanation.surface: A dad of seven children was shown up by a new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father of 7' reads as a man with seven children; it points to Regan, visible inside the answer to 7-down, whose father is Shakespeare's King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to acquire it fully, a verb sense of gaining knowledge through study.

clue.text: Secret op ban "an abomination" admits CEO

indicators.note: admits means the clue words hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: The company chief has conceded calling the banning of a covert operation an outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like a confession by the CEO but signals letters held within 'Secret op ban an abomination'.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal slang for the boss or most important person, as a chief executive is.

clue.text: Doctor Thorne's a crafted period piece

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The TV adaptation of Trollope's Doctor Thorne is a well-made costume drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Thorne' is a Trollope novel, but 'Doctor' is the signal to rearrange THORNE'S A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheraton is an elegant 18th-century English furniture style, so a Sheraton chair is a handmade antique.

clue.text: Pay no attention to Italian chap down south

indicators.note: down here means lost or knocked off, so the letter for south comes out

parts.note: signore is Italian for a gentleman, mister

explanation.surface: Disregard a man from Italy who has moved to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down south' reads as a location; 'down' is the removal signal, taking S out of SIGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to disregard it deliberately, giving it none of your notice.

clue.text: Head supporting sustainable veg

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: green means environmentally sustainable
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A boss backs eco-friendly vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts BEAN under GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Green beans are a common vegetable, the long slim pods of the French bean plant.

clue.text: Formidable bounce of seamer

indicators.note: bounce suggests the letters jumping about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's delivery rears up off the pitch alarmingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounce' signals rearranging OF SEAMER. A seamer is a cricket bowler who makes the ball deviate off its stitched seam.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that inspires dread or alarm by its power.

clue.text: One used to shoot this month's record

parts.note: inst. (instant) is the old business-letter abbreviation for this month
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A photographer shooting this month's album cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests a camera or gun; it is kicking a football with the top of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Footballers strike the ball with the upper arch of the foot when shooting at goal.

clue.text: Raw, serving elite soldiers on island capture that bloke

indicators.note: capture means the soldiers and island enclose the next piece
on in a down clue means the soldiers sit above the island

parts.note: the SAS is the British army's elite Special Air Service
him refers to a man just mentioned

explanation.surface: Commandos are served raw food while on an island mission to seize a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capture' has the soldiers and the island close around the man; 'Raw, serving' together is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is a Japanese dish of thinly sliced uncooked fish, so a raw serving.

clue.text: Tips of white flower about to become something much darker?

indicators.note: tips means the two end letters of the word white are taken
about means the word flower is turned round

explanation.surface: A white bloom is about to turn a deep dark colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips of' takes WE from white; 'about' reverses FLOWER to REWOLF. A man who turns into a wolf becomes something far darker.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a man transforms into this beast at full moon, a sinister change into a dark creature.

clue.text: Old Baltic capital's mass independent paper folding

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia, on the Baltic
m is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: An old Latvian newspaper is in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' looks like a newspaper and 'folding' like going out of business; together they are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of making shapes by creasing sheets of paper.

clue.text: High quality silver robbery reported

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: reported means the word for robbery is heard rather than seen, giving a written form that sounds the same

parts.note: a raid is a robbery

explanation.surface: A news report of a theft of top-grade silverware.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-grade is the top mark, so anything so rated is first-class or excellent.

clue.text: US elder statesman paying respects to The Queen

parts.note: kissing a hand or ring is a way of paying homage
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A veteran American diplomat bows before the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Kissinger was a long-serving American Secretary of State and a veteran diplomat.

clue.text: Current agreement best

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a deal is an agreement

explanation.surface: The present arrangement is the finest one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is the electrical symbol I, not 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect or most suitable, as in the ideal or best solution.

clue.text: Hearing no noise coming from The Nag's Head?

definitions.text: noise coming from The Nag's Head?

indicators.note: hearing means the word is taken as spoken, giving another spelling of the same sound

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A quiet evening at a pub called the Nag's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nag's Head is a common British pub name; read literally it is a horse's head, from which a horse's cry comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old horse, and the sound made from its mouth is the horse's cry.

clue.text: Send back water, being somewhat green

indicators.note: sending back, as with a dish in a restaurant, means the name is reversed

parts.note: Evian is a brand of French mineral water

explanation.surface: A diner returns bottled water, feeling a little queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests feeling sick; here it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or gullible, and naive describes someone lacking worldly experience.

clue.text: American in favour of new ideas, as previously mentioned

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: new means the word ideas is remade in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A US citizen supports fresh thinking, as noted earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges IDEAS into ESAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal documents use the term for a thing already referred to earlier in the text.

clue.text: Producer of smash hit by Jackson family (group's first)

parts.note: Billie Jean was a 1983 number one by Michael Jackson
kin means family

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of group is used

explanation.surface: A smash-hit song by the Jackson family band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smash hit' reads as a chart success; 'smash' is a tennis shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie Jean King was an American tennis champion whose powerful smashes won many Wimbledon titles.
